verdict.rationale: Agora documents token-based channel joining with its RTC SDK, temporary tokens from the Console for development, an App Certificate behind tokens, and a 'minimal backend-plus-client flow' quickstart, so the core join path exists. The evidence does not show server-side session creation or programmatic minting of scoped tokens from a developer's server. missing for 10: documented server-side session/channel creation, server-side minting of scoped join tokens (role/expiry/channel scoping), an explicit end-to-end server-to-client SDK walkthrough, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow

citations.quote: Build the minimal backend-plus-client flow and get a working voice agent running quickly.
During development and testing, use the Agora Console to generate temporary tokens.
When joining a channel, you have the option to either assign a specific UID to the user or pass `0` or `null` and allow Agora to automatically generate and assign a UID to the user.
